item.text: The dense-kernel search has now proved that no homogeneous single-Conv receptive field with fewer than eight coefficients per relevant input/output pair can fit even the supplied corpus, so the existing 8×1 topology is minimal in that dense formulation. A better scorer-aware route is available, though: ONNX sparse initializers are charged only for stored values by the official code. The same convolution can therefore drop from cost 400 to about 20 if runtime/checker compatibility holds; I’m minimizing the exact nonzero support against all legal generator cases now.

item.text: I found a substantially better exact construction that avoids sparse tensors entirely. A single opset-12 `Einsum` can fuse recoloring and vertical continuation: two 10-element channel vectors encode black/blue → black/red, while one shared 6×30 matrix is supplied twice to form a rank-6 Gram transform over rows. Reusing that initializer is the key—its 180 values are counted once—so the predicted total cost is 200 with zero counted intermediate memory.
